Players with fewer than 50 games played are placed in an \"Unknown\" tier (sometimes called Wood) until the system has enough data to place them accurately."},{"q":"Why are MMR recalculations done periodically?","a":"We periodically recalculate MMR across all uploaded games to improve accuracy. As our algorithms improve and more data is uploaded, recalculation gives all players a more accurate rating. We announce these recalculations when they happen \u2014 check our Reddit posts or GitHub for updates."},{"id":"mmr-change-direction","q":"Why did my MMR go down after a win (or up after a loss)?","a":"Heroes Profile MMR is not an infinitely scaling metric \u2014 it's a measure of your skill relative to everyone else. If your MMR dropped after a win, it means the system detected you were playing against players with significantly lower MMR than yours. The algorithm sees a high-MMR player winning against low-MMR opponents and interprets that as a sign your current rating may be too high, so it nudges it down slightly. The reverse is also true \u2014 losing to much higher-MMR players can push your rating up. This is by design: the system is always trying to find the bracket you truly belong in, not just reward you for winning."},{"q":"What is Hero MMR?","a":"Hero MMR is a per-hero MMR rating. Instead of a single overall rating, you have a different MMR for each hero you play. This rating compares you against other players' performance on that same hero. Being a high-level Storm League player doesn't automatically mean you have a high Hero MMR on a hero you rarely play."}]},{"name":"Global Stats & Data","items":[{"q":"How accurate is the data on Heroes Profile?","a":"The data is only as accurate as the number of replays uploaded to our system. We do not have access to every game played \u2014 only games where players have used our uploader or submitted replays manually. That said, we consistently have one of the largest replay databases in the community, with tens of millions of games."},{"q":"Why are mirror matches excluded from matchup win rates?","a":"When a hero faces itself in a mirror match, the result is always one win and one loss for that hero in the same game. Including mirrors would always push the average win rate toward 50% for every hero, giving you no useful information. Excluding them lets the matchup data actually reflect meaningful competitive dynamics."},{"id":"hero-counters","q":"How do I find counters for a hero?","a":"Open the hero on <a href=\"\/Global\/Matchups\" class=\"link\">Matchups<\/a>, e.g. <a href=\"\/Global\/Matchups\/Li-Ming\" class=\"link\">\/Global\/Matchups\/Li-Ming<\/a>. <strong>Top 5 Threats on Enemies Team<\/strong> shows the heroes that do best against them. In the table, sort by <strong>Win Rate Against<\/strong> that hero: the highest win rates are its counters, and the Difference column shows how much better each hero does against it than usual. Check Games Played Against so a small sample doesn't mislead you. <a href=\"\/Global\/Matchups\/Talents\" class=\"link\">Matchup Talents<\/a> then shows which talents to take into that matchup."},{"q":"How does the Performance Score work?","a":"The Performance Score on match pages is calculated by taking each stat from a game (damage, healing, kills, etc.), ranking all 10 players in that game from best to worst, and assigning a score based on rank position. It is a relative measure within that single game \u2014 not a global benchmark."},{"q":"What do the time frame filters mean (major patch vs. minor patch)?","a":"Major patches on Heroes Profile generally align with hero releases or major reworks, when Blizzard changes the number after the first decimal (e.g. 2.44 \u2192 2.45). Minor patches are the smaller balance updates inside a major patch. The Timeframes filter lists every build under its major and sub patch: tick a heading to take the whole patch, or tick single builds. See the <a href=\"\/FAQ#patch-history\" class=\"link\">patch history<\/a> for what each patch changed."},{"id":"hero-average-stats","q":"Can I see a hero's average in-game stats, like siege damage or hero damage?","a":"Yes, every hero's average per game for a stat is on the <a href=\"\/Global\/Hero\" class=\"link\">Hero Stats<\/a> page:<ol class=\"list-decimal pl-6 my-2 flex flex-col gap-1\"><li>Click <strong>Show Advanced Filters<\/strong> under the filters.<\/li><li>Set <strong>Timeframes<\/strong> to 5 or fewer single builds. The Stat Filter is hidden when a whole major or sub patch is ticked.<\/li><li>Pick the stat in <strong>Stat Filter<\/strong>, e.g. Siege Damage, Hero Damage, Spell Damage, Physical Damage, Healing or Deaths, and click <strong>Filter<\/strong>.<\/li><\/ol>The table and bubble chart then show each hero's average per game for that stat instead of win rate. You can also link straight to it, e.g. <a href=\"\/Global\/Hero?statfilter=siege_damage\" class=\"link\">\/Global\/Hero?statfilter=siege_damage<\/a>. The <a href=\"\/Global\/Talents\" class=\"link\">Talents<\/a> page has the same Stat Filter for talents and builds. A full breakdown of one hero's stats side by side, like the advanced stats on a player's hero page, isn't available globally."},{"q":"Why is global data sometimes empty after a new patch?","a":"Right after Blizzard pushes a patch, there isn't enough uploaded data yet for that patch to display meaningful results. Broaden your timeframe filter to include multiple patches, or check back after a few days once more games have been uploaded."},{"id":"win-chance","q":"What is \"Win Chance\" on talent builds, and how is it different from win rate?","a":"Win Chance is our calculated probability that a full talent build leads to a win, from level 1 through level 20. It is not a simple win rate. Because many games end before level 20, we cannot always see the complete build a player intended to take. We use backend logic to infer what build a player was heading toward based on the talents they did pick, and we factor in both games that reached level 20 and games that did not. This gives a more accurate picture of a build's overall viability than just counting wins in completed games. You can explore build Win Chance on the <a href=\"\/Global\/Talents\" class=\"link\">Global Talents<\/a> page and the <a href=\"\/Global\/Talents\/Builder\" class=\"link\">Talent Builder<\/a>."},{"q":"What does the \"Influence\" stat mean?","a":"Influence is a value between -5000 and 5000 that measures how much a hero actually influences the outcome of games. It takes how far the hero's win rate is above or below 50% and multiplies it by how often the hero is picked in the games where it isn't banned. A hero with a high win rate that is rarely picked will have a lower influence score than a hero with a slightly lower win rate that is picked in most games \u2014 because the second hero is actually shaping more matches. Think of it as win rate weighted by relevance."},{"id":"hero-pages","q":"Where can I see a hero's abilities, talents and base stats?","a":"The <a href=\"\/Heroes\" class=\"link\">Heroes<\/a> page, also under Tools in the top menu, has a page for every hero, such as <a href=\"\/Heroes\/Abathur\" class=\"link\">Abathur<\/a>. It is built from the game files for the current patch and has three tabs: <strong>About<\/strong> (role, difficulty, description, ratings, base stats and lore), <strong>Abilities<\/strong> and <strong>Talents<\/strong>. Hover or tap an ability or talent icon for its full tooltip. The level slider scales health, attack damage and ability numbers to any level from 1 to 30, and the scaling numbers show their per-level rate, e.g. 62 (+4% per level). The links under the tabs open that hero on the stats pages, such as Talent Stats and the Talent Builder, for win rates and builds."},{"q":"What is the Talent Builder?","a":"The <a href=\"\/Global\/Talents\/Builder\" class=\"link\">Talent Builder<\/a> lets you construct a specific talent build and see win rate data for exactly that combination. It's great for comparing two builds head-to-head with real game data."},{"q":"What is the best build for a hero?","a":"Open the hero on <a href=\"\/Global\/Talents\" class=\"link\">Talents<\/a>, e.g. <a href=\"\/Global\/Talents\/Valla\" class=\"link\">\/Global\/Talents\/Valla<\/a>. It defaults to the latest patch. The builds table lists complete level 1 to 20 builds; sort it by <strong>Win Chance<\/strong> and check games played, since a build with few games can look better than it is. <strong>Talent Build Type<\/strong> switches between the most played builds and different early-game paths. The talent table above it shows each talent's win rate on its own, which isn't the same as a full build. To test a combination of your own, use the <a href=\"\/Global\/Talents\/Builder\" class=\"link\">Talent Builder<\/a>."}]},{"name":"Filters","items":[{"q":"How do the filters work?","a":"Change any filters you want, then click <strong>Filter<\/strong> to reload the page with them. On global stats pages, <strong>Show Advanced Filters<\/strong> reveals more: Stat Filter, Hero Level, HP Hero Rank, HP Role Rank, Mirror Matches and, on Hero Stats, Group Size. Global stats pages save your filters in the page link, so you can share or bookmark a filtered page. On mobile, tap <strong>Show Filters<\/strong> to open them."},{"q":"What does the Timeframes filter do?","a":"Timeframes picks which patches the data comes from. Builds are listed under their major patch and sub patch: tick a heading to take the whole patch, or tick single builds. It defaults to the latest patch. See <a href=\"\/FAQ#patch-history\" class=\"link\">patch history<\/a> for what each patch changed."},{"q":"What does the Game Type filter do?","a":"Game Type limits the data to Storm League, Quick Match, ARAM and the other modes. Global stats pages leave out Unranked Draft and Custom games. Profile pages include every game type, and Match History can show Custom games too."},{"q":"What does the Stat Filter do?","a":"On <a href=\"\/Global\/Hero\" class=\"link\">Hero Stats<\/a> and <a href=\"\/Global\/Talents\" class=\"link\">Talents<\/a>, the Stat Filter swaps win rate for the average per game of an in-game stat, such as hero, siege, spell, physical or minion damage, healing, deaths, takedowns, time stunning enemies or merc camp captures. It is under Show Advanced Filters and only shows when Timeframes is 5 or fewer single builds. There is a step-by-step guide under \"Can I see a hero's average in-game stats\" in Global Stats &amp; Data."},{"q":"What do the Regions and Map filters do?","a":"<strong>Regions<\/strong> limits the data to games played in NA, EU, KR or CN. <strong>Map<\/strong> limits it to games on the maps you pick."},{"q":"What do the Heroes and Role filters do?","a":"They limit the data to one hero or one role. On <a href=\"\/Match\/Search\" class=\"link\">Replay Search<\/a> you can pick several heroes and choose <strong>OR<\/strong> (games with any of them) or <strong>AND<\/strong> (games with all of them)."},{"q":"What do the HP Player Rank, HP Hero Rank and HP Role Rank filters do?","a":"They filter by skill using Heroes Profile's own MMR: the player's overall MMR, their MMR on that specific hero, or their MMR on that hero's role. The tiers mirror the in-game ones but use our formula, so they won't match in-game ranks. The MMR &amp; Rankings section explains how our MMR works. On Hero Stats and Talents the player one is called <strong>Player Rank<\/strong> and sits with the main filters, with an HP \/ In-Game switch."},{"q":"What is the HP \/ In-Game switch on Player Rank?","a":"On Hero Stats and Talents, Player Rank can use either Heroes Profile MMR tiers (HP) or the Storm League rank Blizzard shows on the loading screen (In-Game). To see a hero's win rate in an in-game league, like Silver, switch it to In-Game, pick the league and click Filter. In-game rank is read by players using the Heroes Profile uploader's opt-in rank reader, and each player counts in the rank they had going into that game. Only players whose rank was read count, so sample sizes are smaller, and only patches since the rank reader started are listed in Timeframes."},{"q":"What does the Hero Level filter do?","a":"Hero Level only includes players who had that hero at the levels you pick, from 1-5 up to 100+. Use it to see how a hero does in experienced hands."},{"q":"What does the Mirror Matches filter do?","a":"It decides whether games with the same hero on both teams count. It defaults to Exclude, because a hero playing itself always adds one win and one loss, pulling its win rate toward 50%."},{"q":"What does the Group Size filter do?","a":"Group Size limits the data to players who queued Solo, as a Duo, or in a group of 3, 4 or 5. On the <a href=\"\/Global\/Party\" class=\"link\">Party<\/a> page, <strong>Team One Party<\/strong> and <strong>Team Two Party<\/strong> pick each team's whole makeup instead, from 5 Solos to a 5 Stack."},{"q":"What does the Minimum Games filter do?","a":"It hides rows with fewer games than the number you pick, so small samples don't crowd the top of the table."},{"q":"What does Talent Build Type do?","a":"It picks which builds the Talents page lists. Only builds that reached level 20 count.<ul class=\"list-disc pl-6 mt-2 flex flex-col gap-1\"><li><strong>Popular<\/strong>: the most played builds.<\/li><li><strong>HP Algorithm<\/strong>: the most played builds, but only one per combination of level 1, 4 and 7 talents, so you see different early-game paths.<\/li><li><strong>Unique Lvl X<\/strong>: the most played build for each different talent at that level.<\/li><\/ul>"},{"q":"What do the Season and date filters do?","a":"<strong>Season<\/strong> limits the data to games in the seasons you pick, grouped by year. On profile pages you can pick several. The <strong>date range<\/strong> filter limits it to games played between the dates you choose."},{"q":"What do the Leaderboard Type and League filters do?","a":"On the <a href=\"\/Global\/Leaderboard\" class=\"link\">Leaderboards<\/a>, Leaderboard Type switches between Player, Hero, Role, Match Prediction and SL Rank boards. SL Rank lists in-game Storm League ranks and adds a League picker."},{"q":"What filters does Replay Search have?","a":"<a href=\"\/Match\/Search\" class=\"link\">Replay Search<\/a> adds a few of its own: <strong>Game Version<\/strong> (patches), a <strong>date range<\/strong>, ranges on <strong>HP Player, Hero and Role MMR<\/strong>, and <strong>Players<\/strong>, which only finds games with those BattleTags in them. Match History has a similar <strong>Friend or Foe Player<\/strong> search."},{"q":"What filters do the esports pages have?","a":"Esports pages have filters for that league instead, such as Season, Division, Team or Tournament, depending on what the league tracks."}]},{"name":"Site Features","items":[{"q":"What is the PreMatch feature?","a":"PreMatch is a feature built into the <a href=\"https:\/\/github.com\/Heroes-Profile\/HeroesProfile.Uploader\/releases\/latest\/download\/HeroesProfileUploaderSetup.exe\" class=\"link\">Heroes Profile Uploader<\/a>. When enabled, it opens a browser page during the loading screen of a match showing information about all 10 players in your game \u2014 their stats, most-played heroes, MMR, and more. This helps you understand your teammates and opponents before the match starts. You can see an example at <a href=\"\/PreMatch\/Results\/\" class=\"link\">PreMatch Results<\/a>."},{"q":"What is the Friends & Foes page?","a":"The Friends &amp; Foes page on your player profile shows your win rate when playing <em>with<\/em> or <em>against<\/em> specific players. For example, see <a href=\"\/Player\/Zemill\/67280\/1\/FriendFoe\" class=\"link\">this Friends &amp; Foes page<\/a>. Upload your replays and check the Friends &amp; Foes section of your own profile to see yours."},{"q":"What is the Awards page?","a":"The Awards page on your player profile shows how often you earn each end of match award, such as MVP, Painbringer or Main Healer, as a percentage of your games. For example, see <a href=\"\/Player\/Zemill\/67280\/1\/Awards\" class=\"link\">this Awards page<\/a>. Click an award to list every game where you earned it. Awards are only counted for games played after Heroes Profile began tracking them, so very old replays are not included. Every award and what it is given for is listed under <a href=\"#awards\" class=\"link\">Match Awards<\/a> below."},{"q":"Can I download a replay file?","a":"Yes. Open the game's match page, from Match History, Replay Search or any match list, and click <strong>Download Replay<\/strong> next to the map and game length. You need to be logged in with Battle.net, and the button is not shown on mobile. You can download up to 100 replays a day, which resets at midnight UTC. Replay files are kept for a limited time, so very old games may not have the button."},{"q":"What is Replay Search and how do I use it?","a":"<a href=\"\/Match\/Search\" class=\"link\">Replay Search<\/a> finds recent games uploaded to Heroes Profile. Pick your filters, press Filter, and each result links to its full match page.<p class=\"mt-2\"><b>What it searches<\/b><\/p><ul class=\"list-disc list-inside mt-1 space-y-1\"><li>Games played in the current and previous season, newest first.<\/li><li>Quick Match, Storm League and ARAM. Unranked Draft, Hero League and Team League have no games in that window.<\/li><li>Results come 1000 at a time. Use <b>Load 1000 More<\/b> to see older games.<\/li><\/ul><p class=\"mt-2\"><b>Filters<\/b><\/p><ul class=\"list-disc list-inside mt-1 space-y-1\"><li><b>Game Type, Regions, Map, Game Version, From\/To Date<\/b>: narrow to those games. Game Version only lists patches from the search window.<\/li><li><b>Heroes<\/b>: pick one or more. With several, the <b>OR \/ AND<\/b> switch chooses between games with any of them or games with every one of them, on either team.<\/li><li><b>Players<\/b>: type a BattleTag and press Add. If several accounts match, choose the right one. Private profiles cannot be searched for. With several players, <b>OR \/ AND<\/b> works the same way as heroes.<\/li><\/ul><p class=\"mt-2\"><b>Advanced Filters<\/b><\/p><ul class=\"list-disc list-inside mt-1 space-y-1\"><li><b>HP Player, Hero and Role MMR<\/b> minimum and maximum, using the rating each player had in that game.<\/li><li><b>HP Player, Hero and Role Rank<\/b> (Bronze to Master). Ranks use the current league boundaries for each game type. HP Hero Rank appears once you pick a hero, since each hero has its own boundaries.<\/li><li>Every MMR and rank filter must hold for the <em>same<\/em> player. With no heroes picked, that can be anyone in the game. With heroes on OR, it is the player on one of those heroes. With heroes on AND, the player on every chosen hero has to meet them.<\/li><\/ul><p class=\"mt-2\"><b>Why does it say \"Keep Searching\"?<\/b><\/p><p class=\"mt-1\">Rare combinations, like several heroes all at Master, can take a long time to find. Replay Search looks through a few seconds' worth of games at a time, shows what it found so far and how far back it has searched, and lets you press <b>Keep Searching<\/b> to continue. \"No replays match those filters\" only appears once the whole search window has been checked.<\/p><p class=\"mt-2\"><b>Limits<\/b><\/p><p class=\"mt-1\">To keep the site fast for everyone, searches are limited to 10 per minute, and each Load More or Keep Searching counts as one. If you hit the limit, wait a minute and try again.<\/p>"},{"q":"What is the Match Prediction Game?","a":"The Match Prediction Game lets you look at a draft and try to predict which team will win before seeing the result. It's a fun way to test your game knowledge and see how your predictions compare to the actual outcome."},{"q":"Does Heroes Profile have esports, tournament, series or league stats?","a":"Yes. <a href=\"\/Esports\" class=\"link\">Community Esports<\/a> in the top menu covers community leagues and tournaments: NGS (Nexus Gaming Series), CCL (Community Clash League), Masters Clash, Heroes International, Nut Cup, and HGC and More, which holds past tournaments and series such as HGC. Each has its own teams, players, matches, and hero and talent stats."},{"q":"What is the Heroes Profile Drafter?","a":"The <a href=\"\/Drafter\" class=\"link\">Heroes Profile Drafter<\/a> is a drafting tool that uses Heroes Profile win rate data to help you evaluate compositions during the draft phase. It is not intended to be a perfect predictor \u2014 use it to supplement your draft knowledge and investigate how compositions perform. See the Drafter section below for how it works."},{"q":"Can I copy a talent build from the site into the game?","a":"Yes. On Global Hero pages, the Single Match page, and several other places around the site you will find a \"Copy Build\" button next to talent builds. Clicking it copies the build to your clipboard in a format that Heroes of the Storm accepts, so you can paste it directly into the game's loadout screen."},{"q":"What is \"Marked by the Void\"?","a":"It's the flair from the Xal'atath takeover event. Players who found her eye hidden on the site earned the Mark of the Void, a void eye shown with their name. The event is over, but the flair is permanent. The <a href=\"\/Event\/Xalatath\" class=\"link\">Xal'atath Event Recap<\/a> has the final totals, including how many players earned it, plus the top players and your own contribution."},{"q":"How does the help assistant work?","a":"The help assistant in the bottom-right corner runs on Claude Haiku 5.5, an AI model made by Anthropic. It answers from this FAQ and the list of site pages, plus a daily snapshot of the main stats pages in their default view (latest patch, Storm League, all ranks). Snapshot pages are picked by matching words in your question; there is no vector search, and it can't look anything up live, so it can't see your stats or any filtered view. For those it links you to the page. It needs a Battle.net login and allows 20 questions a day, 25 for Patreon supporters."}]},{"name":"Drafter","items":[{"q":"How do I use the Drafter?","a":"<p>The Drafter is not a perfect predictor of a draft. It was built to investigate and gauge compositions, so use it to supplement your own draft knowledge.<\/p><ol class=\"list-decimal pl-6 mt-2 flex flex-col gap-2\"><li>Open the <a href=\"\/Drafter\" class=\"link\">Drafter<\/a> and choose your filters. Drafter data is Storm League only, from the latest five patches. Narrow filters can leave only a small number of games, so keep an eye on Games Played, Games Banned and Win Rate Confidence in the hero pop-ups.<\/li><li>Choose which team has first pick. Team 1 is on the left and Team 2 is on the right. This only affects how the draft is laid out, so match it to your in-game draft.<\/li><li>Click <strong>Start Draft<\/strong>. The Drafter loads the best options for the current ban or pick and orders them best to worst, left to right and top to bottom. Heroes it considers especially strong at that position get a star. Hover a hero to see its stats.<\/li><li>Click a hero to ban or pick it. The Drafter moves between Team 1 and Team 2 automatically as the draft goes on, and <strong>Undo<\/strong> steps back one pick.<\/li><\/ol><p class=\"mt-2\">The search box and role icons narrow the heroes shown without changing their order. <strong>Show Filters<\/strong> lets you change filters at any point in the draft, and the suggestions for the current pick reload with the new filters.<\/p><p class=\"mt-2\"><strong>Draft With No Data<\/strong> lets you walk through a draft with every hero listed alphabetically and no suggestions.<\/p><p class=\"mt-2\">The Drafter is best used on a computer. It works on mobile, but there is a lot of information to show.<\/p>"},{"q":"How does the Drafter suggest bans?","a":"<p><strong>Bans 1 to 4<\/strong> start from the most banned heroes for your filters, scaled by how often each hero is banned at that specific position in the draft (its <em>Draft Order Pick Rate<\/em>).<\/p><p class=\"mt-2\">For example, say the most banned heroes are D.Va (200 bans), Imperius (150), Chromie (76) and Orphea (25), and at the current position D.Va is banned 5% of the time, Imperius 20%, Chromie 57% and Orphea 2%. Scaling each by its rate gives Chromie 43.3, Imperius 30, D.Va 10 and Orphea 0.5, so the order changes a lot depending on who tends to be banned at that point in the draft.<\/p><p class=\"mt-2\"><strong>Bans 5 and 6<\/strong> work the same way, but also look at the opposing team's composition to find their next best pick and suggest it as a ban.<\/p>"},{"q":"How does the Drafter suggest picks?","a":"<p><strong>Picks 1 and 2<\/strong> use each hero's Influence scaled by its Draft Order Pick Rate. Influence combines win rate with how often a hero is picked or banned.<\/p><p class=\"mt-2\"><strong>Picks 3 to 10<\/strong> use composition data scaled by Draft Order Pick Rate. If the team then picks The Lost Vikings, the Drafter looks for popular compositions that include a Support and a Ranged Assassin instead. So in week 4, a Player leaderboard requires 20 games played that season.<\/li><\/ul>If fewer than 50 players meet the requirements, the games-played requirement is lowered in steps and the extra players are shown in separate groups. See \"Why is the leaderboard split into groups?\" below."},{"q":"Why is the leaderboard split into groups?","a":"Early in a season, or on less-played heroes and party sizes, fewer than 50 players may meet the full games-played requirement. When that happens, the requirement is lowered by one game per week at a time, down to a minimum of 5 games, until at least 50 players qualify. Each step down becomes its own group, and each group shows the number of games it required.<ul class=\"list-disc list-inside mt-2 space-y-1\"><li><strong>Group A<\/strong> met the full requirement.<\/li><li><strong>Group B<\/strong> met the requirement after one step down, <strong>Group C<\/strong> after two, and so on.<\/li><\/ul>Everyone in a higher group ranks above everyone in a lower group, even if their Heroes Profile Rating is lower. Without groups, a player with only a handful of games and a lucky win rate could jump ahead of players who put in the full number of games. Within each group, players are ranked by Heroes Profile Rating as usual, and rank numbers continue from one group to the next."},{"q":"What is the Heroes Profile Rating and how is it calculated?","a":"The HP Rating is a custom score used to rank players on the leaderboard. It is intentionally not a pure MMR ranking \u2014 a pure MMR leaderboard would quickly be dominated by smurfs and players who reach a high MMR and stop playing, making it stale and uninteresting.<br><br>Instead, HP Rating combines three factors: your <strong>MMR<\/strong>, your <strong>win rate<\/strong>, and your <strong>games played<\/strong> for the season \u2014 all scaled relative to other players on that leaderboard. Games played is capped relative to the top players so that spamming games alone cannot carry you to the top. The result rewards players who are actively playing, winning, and performing at a high level. You can see the exact formula by clicking \"Leaderboard Requirements\" on the <a href=\"\/Global\/Leaderboard\" class=\"link\">Leaderboard page<\/a>."},{"q":"Why does Heroes Profile use HP Rating instead of just showing MMR?","a":"A pure MMR leaderboard has a fundamental flaw: once a player reaches a high MMR, it barely changes. That means the same accounts would sit at the top of every leaderboard indefinitely \u2014 especially smurfs, who can artificially inflate MMR and then stop playing. HP Rating solves this by factoring in active play each season. If you stop playing, your ranking falls even if your MMR stays high. There are tangible things you can do to climb: win more games, play consistently throughout the season."},{"q":"Why can I filter leaderboards by party size?","a":"A 5-stack premade team has a significant coordination advantage over solo players. Putting them on the same leaderboard makes it hard for solo players to compete at the top. Filtering by party size (Solo, 2-Stack, 3-Stack, etc.) lets you see how you rank against players who queued under the same conditions as you."},{"q":"When do seasons start and end?","a":"Leaderboards are split by season, using the start and end date of each one. See <a href=\"#season-dates\" class=\"link\">Season Dates<\/a> below for every season so far."},{"q":"Why are some of my games counted in the wrong season?","a":"Replay files don't say which season a game was played in, and Blizzard doesn't publish exact season start times. Heroes Profile sets the start of a new season when we notice it has changed, so the start time we use can be a few hours after the real one. Games you played in that gap are counted in the previous season, which is why your season stats can be a game or two off from what you see in game.<br><br>A game's season is saved when the replay is processed, and leaderboards and other pages are built from that. Moving a season's start time afterwards would leave those games out of sync with the new date, so we don't change season dates once a season has started."},{"q":"When are leaderboards updated?","a":"Leaderboards are recalculated daily, starting at 2am EST.
